# Holding Frame Design for Plug Connector Modules

The holding frame is specifically designed to receive plug connector modules and features a two-part construction consisting of two halves that can be connected to one another. This modular design provides both structural integrity and assembly flexibility, allowing the frame to accommodate various plug connector configurations as needed.

A key feature of this design is that the two halves can be aligned relative to each other in at least two distinct positions. This capability allows for flexible configuration of the holding frame, enabling it to be adapted to different installation requirements or operational states without requiring separate components for each configuration.

To ensure stability and reliability across these different configurations, at least one fixing means is incorporated into the holding frame. This fixing mechanism is specifically designed to secure the two halves in their respective relative positions, preventing unintended movement or separation once the desired configuration has been established.

The fixing mechanism itself is realized through a practical and efficient design: one or two press projections or lugs are molded directly onto the first half of the holding frame. These projections are precisely dimensioned and positioned to correspond with matching recesses located on one or two end faces of the second half. This complementary arrangement ensures a secure and reliable connection between the two components.

The functional advantage of this design becomes apparent during assembly: by pressing the projections or lugs into their corresponding recesses, the two halves can be fixed relative to one another in either an open position or a closed position. This dual-position capability allows the holding frame to be configured according to specific application needs—whether an open configuration is required for certain installation procedures or a closed configuration is needed for final assembly and secure operation. The press-fit mechanism thus provides a simple yet effective means of achieving reliable positional control while maintaining ease of assembly and adjustment.

# Holding Frame for Plug Connector Modules

## Background

In the field of electrical and data connectivity systems, plug connector modules are frequently assembled into holding frames that organize, position, and secure multiple modules within a single housing or panel opening. These frames must reliably retain the modules against mechanical stresses such as vibration, insertion and withdrawal forces, and thermal cycling, while also allowing for straightforward assembly and, where necessary, disassembly or reconfiguration during installation, maintenance, or field servicing.

A persistent challenge in the design of such holding frames lies in achieving secure, stable retention of the frame components themselves—independent of the connector modules they house—without resorting to additional fasteners such as screws, clips, or adhesive elements. Conventional approaches often introduce extra parts count, increase assembly complexity, or fail to provide well-defined intermediate states (for example, a partially closed or "open" configuration) that would allow modules to be inserted or removed conveniently before the frame is locked into its final, closed operating position. There remains a need for a holding frame design that is simple to manufacture, easy to assemble by hand or with minimal tooling, and capable of maintaining distinct, repeatable positional states throughout the assembly process.

## Summary of the Disclosure

The present disclosure addresses these challenges by providing a holding frame configured to securely accommodate and retain one or more plug connector modules. The holding frame is constructed from two separate frame halves—designated herein as a first half and a second half—that are designed to be joined together to form the complete frame structure.

To enable secure and controlled joining of the two halves, the first half is provided with one or more projections or lugs extending from its mating surface. The second half, correspondingly, includes one or more recesses formed to receive these projections or lugs. When the two halves are brought together, the projections engage the recesses in a press-fit manner, creating a mechanical interference that holds the halves in alignment and resists unintended separation.

A key feature of this design is that the press-fit engagement between the projections and recesses is configured to support at least two distinct, mechanically stable positions of the frame halves relative to one another: an open position and a closed position. In the open position, the two halves are joined loosely enough, or engaged at a shallower depth, to permit the insertion or removal of plug connector modules into the space defined between the halves. In the closed position, the projections are seated more deeply or fully within the recesses, drawing the two halves into tight, secure engagement that firmly clamps and retains the plug connector modules in their final operating location within the frame.

## Detailed Description

### General Structure of the Holding Frame

The holding frame comprises two half-frame components that, together, define an enclosure or channel structure suitable for receiving plug connector modules. Each half may be formed as an injection-molded plastic part, a die-cast metal part, or through any other suitable manufacturing process that allows for precise formation of the projections, lugs, and recesses described below. The two halves are generally complementary in shape, such that when joined, they form a complete frame with an interior cavity or set of cavities sized to accommodate the plug connector modules.

### Projections and Recesses

The first half of the holding frame includes one or more projections, which may also be referred to as lugs, extending outward from an inner mating surface of the half. These projections may take the form of pins, ribs, tabs, or other protruding structures, and may be distributed at multiple locations along the mating surface to provide balanced retention force across the frame.

The second half of the holding frame includes corresponding recesses, cavities, or openings positioned to align with the projections on the first half when the two halves are brought into contact. The recesses are dimensioned relative to the projections such that, upon insertion, an interference or friction fit is created between the projection and the walls of the recess. This press-fit relationship generates sufficient holding force to keep the two halves engaged with one another without requiring separate fasteners.

### Two Distinct Positions: Open and Closed

A distinguishing aspect of the disclosed holding frame is the ability of the projection-and-recess arrangement to define and maintain at least two separate, stable engagement positions:

1. **Open Position:** In this configuration, the projections are only partially inserted into the recesses, or engaged with a lesser degree of interference, such that the two halves are loosely connected. This partial engagement is sufficient to keep the halves aligned and prevent them from becoming completely separated or misplaced during handling, while still leaving enough clearance between the halves to allow plug connector modules to be inserted into, or removed from, the frame. The open position is particularly useful during the assembly process, as it allows an installer to position multiple plug connector modules within the frame before final assembly, without the modules being obstructed by a fully closed frame structure.

2. **Closed Position:** Once the plug connector modules have been properly placed within the frame, the two halves can be pressed further together, driving the projections more deeply into the recesses. This deeper engagement increases the interference fit between the projections and recesses, producing a stronger clamping force that draws the two halves tightly together. In the closed position, the plug connector modules are firmly secured within the frame, held in place by the compressive force exerted by the fully engaged halves. This closed configuration represents the final, operational state of the holding frame, suitable for installation into a larger panel, housing, or connector system.

The transition between the open and closed positions can be achieved through simple manual pressure applied to the two halves, without the need for tools, additional fasteners, or complex assembly procedures. The distinct mechanical detents created by the varying engagement depths of the projections within the recesses provide tactile and positional feedback to the installer, indicating when the frame has reached either the open or closed state.

### Advantages of the Disclosed Design

This two-position press-fit design offers several advantages over conventional holding frame arrangements. First, it simplifies the assembly process by allowing plug connector modules to be inserted while the frame is in a partially open, easily accessible state, and then secured simply by pressing the frame halves fully together. Second, the elimination of separate fasteners reduces the overall part count and assembly time, while also reducing the risk of lost or improperly installed fastening hardware. Third, the use of a press-fit mechanism formed directly into the two frame halves allows for a compact, low-profile design that can be manufactured cost-effectively using standard molding or casting techniques.

Additionally, because the projections and recesses are designed to support two distinct mechanical states, the holding frame provides flexibility during installation and potential rework: modules can be more easily inspected, replaced, or reconfigured while the frame is in its open position, and then the frame can be reliably locked into its closed position once the desired module arrangement is finalized. This adaptability makes the disclosed holding frame particularly well-suited for applications where plug connector modules may need to be swapped, added, or removed over the service life of the equipment.

### Variations and Alternative Embodiments

While the disclosure describes projections on the first half engaging recesses on the second half, it is contemplated that the arrangement of projections and recesses could be reversed, distributed across both halves, or implemented using multiple sets of complementary projection-and-recess pairs at different locations around the perimeter of the frame halves to further enhance stability and alignment. The specific geometry of the projections and recesses—including their cross-sectional shape, taper, and depth—may be varied to adjust the retention force required to move between the open and closed positions, allowing the design to be tuned for different module sizes, weights, or environmental requirements.

Overall, the holding frame described herein provides a robust, simple, and cost-effective solution for securely retaining plug connector modules through a two-piece, press-fit design capable of maintaining well-defined open and closed positions throughout the assembly and operational life of the connector system.

# The: The Most Powerful Word You Never Notice

It's the most commonly used word in the English language, yet most of us never give it a second thought. "The" appears in virtually every sentence we speak or write, silently doing its job without demanding recognition.

## A Word of Definition

"The" is what linguists call a definite article. Its purpose is deceptively simple: it points to something specific. Compare "a dog" to "the dog." The first refers to any dog, unspecified and general. The second refers to a particular dog—one we already know about, one that's been mentioned, or one that's uniquely identifiable in context.

This small distinction carries enormous weight. "The" transforms vague possibility into concrete reality. It tells the listener: *you know exactly what I'm talking about.*

## Ancient Origins

The word traces its roots back to Old English, evolving from words like "þe" and "se," which themselves descended from Proto-Germanic demonstratives. Over centuries, various forms merged and simplified until "the" emerged as the standard definite article we use today, gender-neutral and remarkably flexible.

## Everywhere and Invisible

Because "the" is so frequent, we rarely notice it. It's like the air we breathe—essential, constant, and easy to overlook. Yet remove it from a sentence, and things start to feel off. "I saw dog in park" reads awkwardly, missing the specificity and flow that "the" provides.

Writers and speakers rely on this tiny word constantly, using it to guide readers toward shared understanding, to signal familiarity, and to create coherence across sentences and paragraphs.

## A Word Study in Simplicity

Perhaps what's most remarkable about "the" is its lack of complexity. It has no plural form, no possessive case, no variation for gender. It simply is—unchanging, dependable, and endlessly useful.

In a language full of irregular verbs, tricky spellings, and shifting meanings, "the" stands as a quiet constant. It doesn't seek attention, but without it, communication would lose precision, clarity, and grace.

Sometimes, the smallest words carry the greatest weight.

# PATENT DISCLOSURE

## Two-Piece Holding Frame for Plug Connector Modules

In accordance with an exemplary embodiment, a holding frame for retaining one or more plug connector modules comprises a first frame half and a second frame half, the two frame halves being connected to one another along a common edge by a hinge, such that the frame halves are pivotable relative to one another between an open position and a closed position. The hinge may be configured as a film hinge, integrally molded with at least one of the frame halves, or alternatively as a separately formed pivot connection joining the first frame half to the second frame half, permitting the frame to be manufactured as a single, unitary component prior to assembly.

Each of the first and second frame halves defines at least one receiving opening dimensioned to accommodate a plug connector module therein, such that when the frame halves are pivoted into the closed position, the receiving openings of the first and second frame halves align with one another to form a complete module-receiving passage, thereby clamping and retaining the plug connector module between the two frame halves.

To secure the frame halves in a defined open position, at least one first frame half is provided with at least one latching lug, and the second frame half is provided with a corresponding first latching recess arranged such that, when the frame halves are pivoted to a predetermined open angle, the latching lug engages the first latching recess in a press-fit, snap-in manner, thereby releasably retaining the frame halves in the open position to facilitate insertion of the plug connector module.

To secure the frame halves in the closed position, the first frame half further comprises at least one second latching lug, and the second frame half comprises a corresponding second latching recess, positioned such that when the frame halves are pivoted about the hinge into the closed position, the second latching lug engages the second latching recess in a press-fit manner, thereby locking the frame halves together and retaining the plug connector module captively within the aligned receiving openings. The first and second latching lugs may each comprise a resiliently deflectable protrusion having a beveled leading edge and a retaining shoulder, such that upon insertion into the corresponding latching recess, the protrusion deflects elastically to permit passage of the shoulder past an edge of the recess and subsequently springs back to engage the shoulder against the recess edge, thereby preventing inadvertent disengagement of the frame halves from either the open or closed position without application of a deliberate release force.

In a further embodiment, the latching lugs and latching recesses effecting the open-position lock are arranged along a different edge or surface region of the frame halves than the latching lugs and recesses effecting the closed-position lock, so that the two latching mechanisms do not interfere with one another during pivoting movement of the frame halves between the open and closed positions.

The holding frame may be formed as an integrally molded plastic component, such that the first frame half, the second frame half, the hinge, and the plurality of latching lugs and latching recesses are formed together in a single injection molding process, thereby reducing the number of discrete parts required for assembly and simplifying manufacture of the holding frame.

---

*Note: This is a draft disclosure paragraph suitable for inclusion in a patent specification. It should be reviewed and refined by a registered patent attorney or agent to ensure proper claim support, technical accuracy relative to the actual invention, and compliance with applicable patent office formatting requirements before filing.*

# Modular Connector Holding Frame with Alignment Features

## Technical Field

The present disclosure relates to electrical connector assemblies, and more particularly to a modular holding frame configured to retain one or more connector modules, wherein the holding frame comprises two mating frame halves that are alignable and securable to one another through complementary mechanical interface features.

## Background

Connector holding frames are commonly employed to organize, position, and retain a plurality of individual connector modules within a unified housing structure, facilitating simplified installation, mating, and maintenance of electrical or optical connections. Conventional holding frames are frequently formed as unitary structures or require separate fastening hardware, such as screws, clips, or adhesives, to join multiple frame components. Such arrangements can increase assembly complexity, introduce alignment tolerances that are difficult to control, and require additional manufacturing steps or components, thereby increasing overall cost and assembly time.

There exists a need for a holding frame construction that permits reliable, repeatable, and self-aligning assembly of two or more frame portions without requiring separate fasteners, while maintaining structural integrity and dimensional precision suitable for retaining connector modules in a desired spatial arrangement.

## Summary

In accordance with one or more embodiments, a modular connector holding frame is provided, comprising a first frame half and a second frame half configured to be joined together to form a unitary holding frame structure defining one or more module-receiving cavities configured to receive and retain one or more connector modules therein.

The first frame half comprises a first mating face and the second frame half comprises a second mating face, the first mating face and the second mating face being configured to abut one another when the first frame half and the second frame half are assembled together.

The first frame half further comprises one or more press projections extending outwardly from the first mating face, and the second frame half further comprises one or more corresponding recesses formed in the second mating face, the one or more recesses being configured and dimensioned to receive the one or more press projections in a press-fit engagement therein.

In one or more embodiments, engagement of the one or more press projections within the one or more corresponding recesses aligns the first frame half relative to the second frame half in at least one of a lateral direction, a longitudinal direction, and a rotational orientation, such that the module-receiving cavities of the first frame half and the second frame half are brought into registration with one another.

In one or more embodiments, the press-fit engagement between the one or more press projections and the one or more corresponding recesses is configured to generate a retention force sufficient to secure the first frame half to the second frame half in the assembled configuration without requiring additional fastening elements, although supplemental fastening elements may optionally be employed in combination with the press-fit engagement in certain embodiments.

## Detailed Description

### General Configuration

Referring generally to the drawings, wherein like reference numerals refer to like features throughout the several views, there is shown a modular connector holding frame, generally designated by reference numeral 100, comprising a first frame half 110 and a second frame half 120. The first frame half 110 and the second frame half 120 are configured to be assembled together along a mating plane to form the holding frame 100 in an assembled configuration.

The holding frame 100 defines a plurality of module-receiving cavities 130 extending through the holding frame 100, each of the module-receiving cavities 130 being configured to receive and retain a connector module (not shown) therein. In one or more embodiments, the module-receiving cavities 130 are formed cooperatively by a first plurality of partial cavity portions 132 formed in the first frame half 110 and a second plurality of partial cavity portions 134 formed in the second frame half 120, such that when the first frame half 110 and the second frame half 120 are joined together, the first plurality of partial cavity portions 132 align with the second plurality of partial cavity portions 134 to form the complete module-receiving cavities 130.

### Alignment and Retention Features

The first frame half 110 comprises a first mating face 112 configured to confront and abut a second mating face 122 of the second frame half 120 when the holding frame 100 is in the assembled configuration.

Extending outwardly from the first mating face 112 are one or more press projections 140. Each of the press projections 140 may comprise, for example, a post, pin, boss, protrusion, or other raised structural feature suitable for insertion into a corresponding recess. In one or more embodiments, the press projections 140 are integrally formed with the first frame half 110, such as by injection molding, although it is contemplated that the press projections 140 may alternatively be formed as separate components affixed to the first mating face 112.

Formed in the second mating face 122 of the second frame half 120 are one or more recesses 150 corresponding in number, position, and dimension to the one or more press projections 140. Each of the recesses 150 may comprise, for example, a bore, aperture, socket, channel, or other depression suitable for receiving a corresponding press projection 140 therein. In one or more embodiments, the recesses 150 extend partially into the second frame half 120, forming blind bores; in other embodiments, the recesses 150 may extend entirely through the second frame half 120, forming through-holes.

Each press projection 140 is configured with an outer dimension, such as a diameter or cross-sectional width, that is substantially equal to or slightly greater than a corresponding inner dimension of the associated recess 150, such that upon insertion of the press projection 140 into the recess 150, an interference fit is established therebetween. This interference fit generates a frictional and/or mechanical retention force sufficient to resist separation of the first frame half 110 from the second frame half 120 under normal handling and operational loading conditions.

In one or more embodiments, the press projections 140 comprise a tapered or frustoconical leading end 142 configured to facilitate initial insertion and self-centering of the press projection 140 within the corresponding recess 150 prior to full engagement of the interference fit. In one or more embodiments, the press projections 140 may further comprise one or more ribs, splines, or knurled surface features (not shown) disposed along an outer surface thereof, configured to locally deform upon insertion into the recess 150 so as to enhance the retention force while accommodating manufacturing tolerances.

### Alignment Function

In one or more embodiments, at least a subset of the press projections 140 and corresponding recesses 150 are positioned at or near a periphery of the first frame half 110 and second frame half 120, respectively, such that engagement thereof establishes a coarse alignment between the first frame half 110 and the second frame half 120 prior to full seating of the mating faces 112, 122. In one or more embodiments, at least one press projection 140 and corresponding recess 150 pair is provided with a non-circular cross-sectional geometry, such as an oval, polygonal, or keyed shape, so as to prevent relative rotation between the first frame half 110 and the second frame half 120 about an axis of the press projection 140, thereby ensuring correct rotational orientation of the two frame halves during assembly.

In one or more embodiments, a plurality of press projections 140 and corresponding recesses 150 are distributed about the holding frame 100 in a non-symmetric pattern, such that the first frame half 110 and the second frame half 120 may be assembled together in only a single, predetermined relative orientation, thereby preventing incorrect or reversed assembly of the holding frame 100.

### Assembly Method

According to one or more embodiments, a method of assembling the modular connector holding frame 100 comprises the steps of: positioning the first frame half 110 in general alignment with the second frame half 120 such that the one or more press projections 140 are brought into registration with the one or more corresponding recesses 150; applying a compressive force to urge the first frame half 110 and the second frame half 120 together along an assembly axis substantially perpendicular to the mating faces 112, 122; and inserting the one or more press projections 140 into the one or more corresponding recesses 150 to a depth sufficient to establish the interference fit therebetween, thereby securing the first frame half 110 to the second frame half 120 in the assembled configuration and aligning the first plurality of partial cavity portions 132 with the second plurality of partial cavity portions 134 to form the module-receiving cavities 130.

### Alternative Embodiments

It is contemplated that in one or more alternative embodiments, the press projections 140 may be disposed on the second frame half 120 while the corresponding recesses 150 are disposed on the first frame half 110, or that both the first frame half 110 and the second frame half 120 may each comprise a combination of press projections 140 and recesses 150 arranged in a complementary pattern such that engagement of the two frame halves 110, 120 results in simultaneous multi-point alignment and retention.

It is further contemplated that the holding frame 100 may comprise more than two frame portions, such as three or more modular frame segments, each pair of adjacent frame segments being joined via press projections and corresponding recesses substantially as described hereinabove, so as to accommodate a scalable or expandable connector holding frame configuration.

## Claims (Exemplary)

**1.** A modular connector holding frame comprising:
a first frame half comprising a first mating face and one or more press projections extending outwardly from the first mating face; and
a second frame half comprising a second mating face configured to abut the first mating face, and one or more recesses formed in the second mating face and configured to receive the one or more press projections in a press-fit engagement;
wherein the first frame half and the second frame half, when assembled together, define one or more module-receiving cavities configured to retain a connector module therein.

**2.** The modular connector holding frame of claim 1, wherein the press-fit engagement between the one or more press projections and the one or more recesses aligns the first frame half relative to the second frame half such that the module-receiving cavities are brought into registration.

**3.** The modular connector holding frame of claim 1, wherein at least one of the one or more press projections comprises a tapered leading end configured to facilitate self-centering engagement with a corresponding recess.

**4.** The modular connector holding frame of claim 1, wherein at least one of the one or more press projections and a corresponding recess have a non-circular cross-sectional geometry configured to prevent relative rotation between the first frame half and the second frame half.

**5.** The modular connector holding frame of claim 1, wherein the one or more press projections and the one or more recesses are arranged in a non-symmetric pattern configured to permit assembly of the first frame half and the second frame half in only a single predetermined relative orientation.

**6.** The modular connector holding frame of claim 1, wherein the press-fit engagement is configured to secure the first frame half to the second frame half without requiring additional fastening elements.

**7.** A method of assembling a modular connector holding frame, the method comprising:
aligning a first frame half with a second frame half such that one or more press projections extending from a first mating face of the first frame half are in registration with one or more corresponding recesses formed in a second mating face of the second frame half;
applying a compressive force to the first frame half and the second frame half to insert the one or more press projections into the one or more corresponding recesses; and
establishing an interference fit between the one or more press projections and the one or more corresponding recesses sufficient to secure the first frame half to the second frame half and align a plurality of partial cavity portions of the first frame half with a plurality of partial cavity portions of the second frame half to form one or more module-receiving cavities.

---

*Note: This document is drafted in the style of a patent specification for illustrative/educational purposes. Reference numerals, specific dimensional relationships, and claim scope would need to be tailored to the actual invention, prior art landscape, and prosecution strategy in consultation with a registered patent practitioner.*

# Holding Frame Assembly with Connectable Halves and Press-Fit Securing Means

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to a holding frame assembly, and more particularly to a two-part holding frame comprising a pair of connectable frame halves configured to releasably secure an object therein, wherein the frame halves are joined by at least one fixing means and are selectively retainable in an open position and a closed position by means of a plurality of press-fit lugs engaging corresponding recesses.

## Background of the Invention

Holding frames of various constructions are known in the art for retaining articles such as panels, plates, display items, or other objects requiring peripheral support. Conventional frames of this type typically comprise a unitary structure or a plurality of components joined by separate fasteners such as screws, bolts, or clips. Such arrangements often require tools for assembly and disassembly, and frequently fail to provide a stable intermediate or fully open configuration suitable for insertion or removal of the held object. There exists a need for a holding frame that may be readily transitioned between an open configuration, permitting access to receive or release an object, and a closed configuration, in which the object is securely retained, without the use of separate tools, while nevertheless providing a positive, tactile, and mechanically stable engagement in each of said configurations.

## Summary of the Invention

According to one aspect of the present invention, there is provided a holding frame comprising:

a first frame half and a second frame half, each of the first frame half and the second frame half having an inner surface, an outer surface, and at least one edge region;

at least one fixing means connecting the first frame half to the second frame half such that the first frame half and the second frame half are pivotable, slidable, or otherwise displaceable relative to one another between an open position and a closed position;

wherein the first frame half and/or the second frame half further comprise a plurality of press-fit lugs projecting from the inner surface or the edge region thereof; and

wherein the first frame half and/or the second frame half further comprise a plurality of recesses formed in the inner surface or the edge region thereof, each of the plurality of recesses being positioned and configured to receivingly engage a corresponding one of the plurality of press-fit lugs in a press-fit engagement;

wherein a first set of the plurality of recesses is arranged to receive the plurality of press-fit lugs when the first frame half and the second frame half are disposed in the open position, thereby releasably retaining the holding frame in the open position; and

wherein a second set of the plurality of recesses is arranged to receive the plurality of press-fit lugs when the first frame half and the second frame half are disposed in the closed position, thereby releasably retaining the holding frame in the closed position.

In accordance with a further aspect of the invention, the press-fit lugs each comprise a rounded, chamfered, or frustoconical leading portion configured to facilitate camming engagement into a corresponding recess upon application of a manually applied closing or opening force, and a retention shoulder configured to resist inadvertent withdrawal of the lug from the recess absent the application of a deliberate separating force exceeding a predetermined threshold.

## Detailed Description of the Invention

### General Configuration

Referring generally to the invention, the holding frame comprises two frame halves, designated herein as a first frame half and a second frame half, each of which may be fabricated from a rigid or semi-rigid material including, without limitation, injection-molded plastic, metal, or a composite material. The first frame half and the second frame half are dimensioned and configured such that, when brought together, they cooperatively define an interior region suitable for receiving and retaining an object therein, such as, by way of non-limiting example, a panel, card, plate, photograph, nameplate, sign, electronic component, or similar article.

### The Fixing Means

The first frame half and the second frame half are joined to one another by at least one fixing means. In accordance with certain embodiments, the fixing means comprises a hinge structure, which may be integrally molded as a living hinge, or may comprise a separately formed hinge pin, axle, or pivot element disposed at or adjacent a common edge of the first frame half and the second frame half, such that the first frame half and the second frame half are pivotable relative to one another about a pivot axis defined by the fixing means.

In alternative embodiments, the fixing means may comprise a sliding track and cooperating rail, a flexible tether or strap, a resilient connecting web, or any other mechanical connector suitable for permitting relative displacement between the first frame half and the second frame half between the open position and the closed position, while preventing complete separation of the first frame half from the second frame half during normal use.

It will be appreciated that, in certain embodiments, a plurality of fixing means may be provided, disposed at spaced-apart locations along the common edge of the first frame half and the second frame half, so as to distribute mechanical stress and enhance the structural integrity of the connection therebetween.

### The Press-Fit Lugs and Recesses

In accordance with the invention, at least one of the first frame half and the second frame half comprises a plurality of press-fit lugs projecting outwardly from a surface thereof. Each press-fit lug preferably comprises a body portion extending from the surface of the respective frame half, and a distal engagement portion configured for press-fit, snap-fit, or interference-fit engagement within a correspondingly configured recess formed in the opposing frame half.

Each recess is preferably configured with an internal dimension slightly smaller than, or substantially corresponding to, an external dimension of the distal engagement portion of the corresponding press-fit lug, such that engagement of the press-fit lug within the recess is achieved by the application of a modest manually applied force, and such that the press-fit lug, once seated within the recess, is retained therein by frictional and/or interference forces sufficient to resist unintended disengagement under normal handling conditions, yet insufficient to prevent deliberate disengagement by a user applying a separating force.

In a preferred embodiment, the plurality of press-fit lugs and the plurality of recesses are arranged in at least two complementary sets:

1. **A first set**, positioned such that, when the first frame half and the second frame half are pivoted, slid, or otherwise displaced into the open position, the press-fit lugs of the first frame half (or the second frame half) engage the corresponding recesses of the first set, thereby yieldably retaining the first frame half and the second frame half in the open position against inadvertent closure;

2. **A second set**, positioned such that, when the first frame half and the second frame half are pivoted, slid, or otherwise displaced into the closed position, the press-fit lugs engage the corresponding recesses of the second set, thereby yieldably retaining the first frame half and the second frame half in the closed position against inadvertent opening.

It is to be understood that the number, size, shape, and arrangement of the press-fit lugs and corresponding recesses may be varied according to the particular application, the size of the holding frame, and the anticipated forces to which the holding frame will be subjected in use, without departing from the scope of the present invention.

### Operation

In use, a user positions the first frame half and the second frame half in the open position, wherein the press-fit lugs are engaged within the first set of recesses, thereby holding the holding frame in a stable open configuration suitable for the insertion of an object to be held. The user then applies a closing force to the first frame half and/or the second frame half, causing the press-fit lugs to disengage from the first set of recesses, permitting relative displacement of the first frame half and the second frame half about or along the fixing means, until the press-fit lugs engage the second set of recesses, whereupon the holding frame is retained in the closed position, securing the object therein.

Reversal of the above steps permits the user to return the holding frame to the open position for removal or replacement of the held object, without the necessity of tools or separate fasteners.

### Advantages

The holding frame of the present invention provides several advantages over frames known in the art, including, without limitation: (i) tool-free assembly and disassembly; (ii) a positive tactile indication to the user upon achievement of the open position and the closed position, respectively; (iii) enhanced structural stability in both the open position and the closed position by virtue of the press-fit engagement between the lugs and the recesses; and (iv) reduced part count and manufacturing complexity, insofar as the press-fit lugs and recesses may be integrally formed with the respective frame halves during a molding or forming process.

---

*It should be understood that the foregoing detailed description is provided by way of example only, and that various modifications may be made without departing from the spirit and scope of the invention as defined by the appended claims.*

## Exemplary Claims

**1.** A holding frame comprising:
a first frame half and a second frame half;
at least one fixing means connecting said first frame half to said second frame half, permitting relative displacement therebetween between an open position and a closed position;
a plurality of press-fit lugs disposed on one of said first frame half and said second frame half; and
a plurality of recesses disposed on the other of said first frame half and said second frame half, said plurality of recesses comprising a first set configured to receive said plurality of press-fit lugs when said first frame half and said second frame half are in said open position, and a second set configured to receive said plurality of press-fit lugs when said first frame half and said second frame half are in said closed position.

**2.** The holding frame of claim 1, wherein said at least one fixing means comprises a hinge.

**3.** The holding frame of claim 2, wherein said hinge comprises a living hinge integrally formed with at least one of said first frame half and said second frame half.

**4.** The holding frame of claim 1, wherein each of said plurality of press-fit lugs comprises a chamfered leading portion and a retention shoulder.

**5.** The holding frame of claim 1, wherein said first frame half and said second frame half are configured to cooperatively define an interior region for receiving an object upon disposition in said closed position.

**6.** The holding frame of claim 1, wherein said plurality of press-fit lugs and said plurality of recesses are integrally molded with said first frame half and said second frame half, respectively.

# ELECTRICAL CONNECTOR HOLDING FRAME ASSEMBLY

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present disclosure relates generally to electrical connector systems, and more particularly to a two-piece holding frame assembly for retaining and securing electrical connectors, wherein the frame halves are joined through an integrally molded press-fit engagement mechanism.

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Electrical connector holding frames are commonly employed to secure connector housings within panels, chassis, or other mounting structures. Conventional holding frames often require separate fastening hardware, such as screws, clips, or adhesives, to join the frame components together. Such additional fastening elements increase assembly time, manufacturing cost, and component count, while also introducing potential points of mechanical failure or loosening due to vibration over the operational life of the connector assembly.

There exists a need for a holding frame design that provides secure, reliable retention of its constituent parts without reliance on ancillary fasteners, while maintaining ease of assembly and structural integrity suitable for use in electrical connector applications.

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

According to one aspect of the present disclosure, an electrical connector holding frame is provided, comprising a first frame half and a second frame half configured to mate with one another to define an enclosed housing for retaining at least one electrical connector.

The first frame half includes a body portion having an inner surface, an outer surface, and at least one aperture configured to receive and retain a terminal end of an electrical connector. Integrally formed on the inner surface of the first frame half are one or more press lugs, each press lug comprising a raised protrusion extending substantially perpendicular to the inner surface and terminating in an engagement head having a cross-sectional dimension greater than a shank portion connecting the engagement head to the inner surface.

The second frame half likewise includes a body portion having an inner surface and an outer surface, and defines one or more recesses formed in the inner surface thereof, the recesses being positioned and dimensioned to correspond to the one or more press lugs of the first frame half. Each recess includes an entry opening and an internal cavity, the internal cavity having a cross-sectional dimension substantially matching or slightly exceeding the cross-sectional dimension of the engagement head of the corresponding press lug, such that upon insertion, the engagement head is retained within the internal cavity through an interference or snap-fit engagement.

In assembly, the first frame half and second frame half are brought into mating alignment such that the press lugs are inserted into the corresponding recesses. Upon full insertion, the engagement heads pass through the entry openings, which may be dimensioned with a slightly reduced cross-section relative to the engagement heads to provide a resilient, deflection-based retention force, thereby securing the two frame halves together in a fixed relationship without requiring additional fasteners.

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION

### General Configuration

Referring generally to the structure of the holding frame assembly, the assembly comprises two complementary frame halves, designated herein as a first frame half and a second frame half, which cooperate to form a unified holding frame structure suitable for receiving, positioning, and securing one or more electrical connectors therein.

Each frame half may be fabricated from a molded plastic material, such as a thermoplastic resin, through an injection molding process, allowing the press lugs and corresponding recesses to be formed integrally with the body of each respective frame half during a single molding operation. This integral formation eliminates the need for separately manufactured fastening components and reduces overall part count.

### First Frame Half and Press Lug Structure

The first frame half comprises a generally planar or contoured body having a peripheral wall extending therefrom to define, in part, an internal cavity for receiving an electrical connector. Disposed at one or more locations along the inner surface of the first frame half are press lugs, which project from the inner surface in a direction generally toward the second frame half when the assembly is in a mated configuration.

Each press lug may comprise a shank portion extending from the inner surface and an enlarged engagement head disposed at a distal end of the shank portion, remote from the inner surface. The engagement head may be configured with a rounded, barbed, conical, or bulbous profile such that the head presents a maximum cross-sectional dimension greater than that of the shank portion. In certain embodiments, the press lug may further include one or more longitudinal slots or slits extending from the distal end of the engagement head toward the shank portion, thereby imparting a degree of resilience or compressibility to the engagement head to facilitate insertion into a correspondingly dimensioned recess.

The number, size, and placement of the press lugs may be selected based on the size and configuration of the electrical connector to be retained, as well as anticipated mechanical loading conditions, and may be arranged in a symmetric or asymmetric pattern about the periphery of the first frame half to ensure balanced retention forces.

### Second Frame Half and Recess Structure

The second frame half comprises a body configured to mate with the first frame half and cooperatively define the internal cavity of the holding frame assembly. Formed in the inner surface of the second frame half are one or more recesses, each recess being positioned in registration with a corresponding press lug of the first frame half when the two frame halves are brought into a mated orientation.

Each recess may comprise an entry opening disposed at the inner surface of the second frame half and communicating with an internal cavity formed within the body of the second frame half. The internal cavity is dimensioned to receive the engagement head of the corresponding press lug, and the entry opening may be dimensioned with a cross-sectional dimension smaller than that of the engagement head, such that the engagement head must undergo elastic deformation, or cause elastic deformation of the material surrounding the entry opening, in order to pass therethrough during assembly.

Upon passage of the engagement head through the entry opening, the engagement head enters the internal cavity and, due to the resilient properties of the molded material, returns substantially to its original configuration, thereby becoming captured within the internal cavity. The engagement head is thus prevented from withdrawal through the entry opening by the shoulder formed at the transition between the entry opening and the internal cavity, providing a positive mechanical lock between the first frame half and the second frame half.

### Alternative Embodiments

In certain alternative embodiments, the press lugs may be provided on the second frame half, with the corresponding recesses formed in the first frame half, without departing from the scope of the present disclosure. Further, it is contemplated that a combination of press lugs and recesses may be provided on both the first frame half and the second frame half, such that certain connection points employ press lugs extending from the first frame half into recesses of the second frame half, while other connection points employ press lugs extending from the second frame half into recesses of the first frame half, thereby providing enhanced retention symmetry and resistance to separation under multi-directional loading.

In further embodiments, the press lugs and recesses may be provided with keying features, such as non-circular cross-sections or asymmetric profiles, to ensure that the first frame half and second frame half may be assembled in only one correct relative orientation, thereby preventing incorrect assembly and ensuring proper alignment of connector-receiving apertures.

### Assembly and Operation

In use, an electrical connector or connectors are positioned within the internal cavity defined by the first frame half. The second frame half is then brought into alignment with the first frame half such that each press lug is aligned with its corresponding recess. An assembly force is then applied to urge the first frame half and second frame half together, causing each press lug to be inserted into its corresponding recess.

As each press lug is inserted, the engagement head thereof passes through the entry opening of the corresponding recess, temporarily deforming either the engagement head, the material surrounding the entry opening, or both, until the engagement head is received within the internal cavity of the recess. Upon reaching the internal cavity, the deformed portions substantially return to their original shape, thereby locking the engagement head within the internal cavity and securing the first frame half to the second frame half.

The resulting assembled holding frame provides a unified structure that securely retains the electrical connector or connectors therein, resists separation of the first and second frame halves under normal operating conditions, and may be disassembled, in certain embodiments, through application of a sufficient separating force to again deform the engagement heads and permit withdrawal thereof from the corresponding recesses, if disassembly or connector servicing is desired.

## CLAIMS (Illustrative, Non-Limiting)

**1.** An electrical connector holding frame assembly comprising:
a first frame half having an inner surface and at least one press lug integrally formed on and projecting from the inner surface, the press lug comprising a shank portion and an engagement head disposed at a distal end of the shank portion, the engagement head having a cross-sectional dimension greater than a cross-sectional dimension of the shank portion; and
a second frame half configured to mate with the first frame half, the second frame half having an inner surface defining at least one recess formed therein and positioned in registration with the press lug, the recess comprising an entry opening and an internal cavity, the internal cavity dimensioned to receive and retain the engagement head of the press lug upon insertion thereof through the entry opening.

**2.** The assembly of claim 1, wherein the entry opening of the recess has a cross-sectional dimension smaller than the cross-sectional dimension of the engagement head, such that insertion of the press lug into the recess causes temporary elastic deformation of at least one of the engagement head and a portion of the second frame half surrounding the entry opening.

**3.** The assembly of claim 1, wherein the first frame half and the second frame half are each formed as a single molded piece of thermoplastic material, with the press lug and the recess, respectively, formed integrally therewith.

**4.** The assembly of claim 1, wherein a plurality of press lugs are disposed on the inner surface of the first frame half at spaced-apart locations, and a corresponding plurality of recesses are disposed on the inner surface of the second frame half in registration therewith.

**5.** The assembly of claim 1, wherein the press lug further comprises at least one longitudinal slot extending from the engagement head toward the shank portion to impart resilience to the engagement head.

**6.** The assembly of claim 1, wherein the first frame half and the second frame half, when mated, define an internal cavity configured to receive and retain at least one electrical connector therein.

---

*It is to be understood that the foregoing description and accompanying claims are illustrative of the principles of the invention and are not intended to limit the scope thereof to the specific embodiments disclosed. Various modifications, substitutions, and alterations may be made without departing from the spirit and scope of the invention as defined by the appended claims.*

# Holding Frame Assembly for Plug Connector Modules

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to electrical connector systems, and more particularly to a holding frame (also referred to as a module carrier or frame housing) for receiving and retaining a plurality of plug connector modules, wherein the holding frame is constructed from two frame half-shells that are joined together by a snap-fit connection permitting fixation in a plurality of discrete relative positions.

---

## Background

Modular plug connector systems are widely used in industrial, data transmission, and power distribution applications, where a common outer holding frame accommodates individual, interchangeable connector modules (e.g., signal, data, pneumatic, or power modules). The holding frame must securely retain these modules while itself being mountable into a panel cutout, connector hood, or housing wall.

A recurring design challenge is that holding frames of a given nominal size must often accommodate varying numbers or combinations of modules, module widths, or coding configurations. Conventional one-piece frames are dimensionally fixed and therefore require a distinct part number for every frame length or module-count variant, increasing tooling and inventory costs.

There is accordingly a need for a holding frame architecture that:

1. Is composed of a minimal number of identical or complementary parts;
2. Can be reconfigured, during assembly, to different lengths or module-receiving capacities using the same base components;
3. Provides a secure, tool-less, and reliably positioned joint between its constituent parts, avoiding the need for separate fasteners; and
4. Maintains mechanical stability and electrical/EMC shielding continuity across the joint in all supported configurations.

---

## Summary of the Invention

The invention provides a holding frame for plug connector modules, comprising a **first frame half** and a **second frame half**, each preferably being U-shaped or channel-shaped in cross section and each defining one or more module-receiving compartments bounded by transverse partition walls.

The first frame half and second frame half are joined to one another along a mating interface such that they together enclose a module-receiving space. According to the invention, the joining is achieved by a **snap-connection arrangement** comprising:

- One or more **press (snap) projections** — resilient, cantilevered, or wedge-shaped protrusions formed integrally on a first joining wall of one frame half; and
- A corresponding plurality of **recesses** (snap pockets, latch openings, or detent slots) arranged in a row or array along a second joining wall of the other frame half, spaced apart from one another by a defined pitch distance.

Because the recesses are provided in a **series of at least two, and preferably three or more**, positioned at regular intervals along the joining wall, the press projection(s) of the first frame half can be selectively engaged with any one (or any selected subset) of the available recesses. This allows the two frame halves to be joined at **multiple discrete relative positions** relative to one another along the longitudinal (or transverse) direction of the frame, thereby varying the overall assembled length of the holding frame and/or the number and size of module-receiving compartments, while employing only two basic (optionally identical) half-frame components.

The snap projections and recesses are dimensioned so that, in every one of the available relative positions, a positive mechanical latch is formed, holding the two frame halves together against separation forces encountered during shipping, module insertion/removal, and normal service handling, without requiring screws, rivets, or adhesives.

---

## Detailed Description

### 1. General Structure of the Holding Frame

The holding frame (10) comprises a first frame half (20) and a second frame half (30). Each frame half is preferably manufactured as a single injection-molded part from a fiber-reinforced thermoplastic (e.g., PBT, PA66, or a metallized/EMC-shielded variant), and each has:

- A **base wall** (22, 32) extending in a longitudinal direction (X);
- Two **longitudinal side walls** (24, 34) extending perpendicularly from the base wall to form a channel or trough cross-section;
- A plurality of **transverse partition webs** (26, 36) projecting inward from the side walls, spaced along the longitudinal direction so as to define individual module-receiving compartments (28, 38), each compartment sized to receive one standardized plug connector module;
- At the free longitudinal end of each frame half, a **joining wall** or **joining tongue** (25, 35) extending in the longitudinal direction, configured to overlap or abut the corresponding joining wall of the other frame half when assembled.

In the assembled condition, the first frame half and second frame half are arranged end-to-end (or, in an alternative embodiment, face-to-face in a "clamshell" configuration) such that their compartments together form a continuous row of module-receiving stations, and the joining walls overlap one another along a common overlap region.

### 2. Press Projections

The first frame half's joining wall (25) carries one or more **press projections (40)**. Each press projection is preferably formed as:

- A **ramped, resilient latch lug** projecting from the outer or inner face of the joining wall, having a leading insertion ramp (angled surface, e.g., 20°–45° relative to the plane of the wall) and a trailing, substantially perpendicular **latch shoulder** (42);
- Alternatively, a **rigid press nub or dome** intended to seat into a correspondingly shaped recess, relying on the resilience of the surrounding wall material (rather than a cantilever beam) to permit snap-through; and
- Optionally reinforced by a lateral **guide rib** on either side, to prevent lateral (transverse) shifting once seated, and to guide the mating wall during assembly.

In one preferred embodiment, two press projections are provided on the joining wall, laterally spaced apart at a distance corresponding to the width of the side walls, so that one projection engages a recess proximate each side wall — improving resistance to twisting/racking of the joint.

### 3. Recess Array

The second frame half's joining wall (35) is formed with a **linear or curvilinear array of recesses (50a, 50b, 50c, …, 50n)**, where n ≥ 2. The recesses are preferably:

- Through-openings (windows) or blind pockets molded into the joining wall;
- Spaced at a uniform pitch (P) corresponding to an integer submultiple of the standard module width (W), e.g., P = W, P = W/2, such that engagement at successive recesses shifts the relative position of the two frame halves by one module width or a fraction thereof;
- Each shaped with an internal latch edge or shoulder (52) configured to mate with the latch shoulder (42) of the press projection, forming a positive, self-locking engagement upon full insertion;
- Each recess entrance chamfered or flared to guide the press projection into engagement and to accommodate the ramped insertion surface, allowing snap-through with an audible/tactile click upon reaching the seated position.

The number and pitch of recesses is selected according to the intended range of module-count configurations to be supported by the given frame size — for example, a frame intended to hold between 2 and 6 modules may provide four or five recesses in the array, permitting the assembled frame to be configured to hold 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6 modules total by selecting the corresponding recess for engagement.

### 4. Multiple Fixation Positions

Because the press projection(s) can be inserted into and latched within **any one of the plurality of recesses**, the two frame halves may be fixed relative to one another in a corresponding plurality of discrete relative positions, differing by the pitch distance P (or a multiple thereof, if more than one press projection/recess pair is engaged simultaneously).

This has the following advantageous consequences:

- **Overall length adjustability:** The overall installed length of the holding frame, and hence the number of module compartments effectively enclosed, can be adapted at the point of assembly, without requiring differently sized frame halves for each configuration.
- **Compartment count/size adaptability:** Where partition webs are provided at fixed intervals on each half, selecting a different recess changes which partition webs of the first half align with which of the second half, effectively allowing compartments to be "merged" (by omitting an internal partition at the joint) or kept discrete, permitting mixed-width module acceptance (e.g., double-width modules spanning a joint).
- **Tolerance/positional compensation:** Selection among adjacent recesses (fine pitch) permits compensation for accumulated manufacturing tolerances, ensuring accurate alignment of the assembled frame within its receiving housing or panel cutout, regardless of which particular relative position is used.
- **Common part number / reduced tooling:** A single injection mold for each frame half can serve multiple assembled-frame variants, reducing the number of unique parts, tooling investment, and inventory complexity.

### 5. Latching/Retention Detail

In the preferred embodiment, the press projection (40) is a cantilevered snap arm formed integrally with the joining wall (25), extending substantially in the longitudinal (insertion) direction, terminating in a latch head having:

- A **lead-in bevel** facing the direction of insertion, causing the arm to deflect elastically inward (or the receiving wall to deflect outward) as the frame halves are brought together;
- A **latch shoulder** perpendicular (or slightly undercut, e.g., 5°–15° negative draft) to the insertion direction, which — upon the latch head clearing the recess opening — snaps back to its relaxed position and engages the recess's internal edge (52), preventing withdrawal;
- Optionally, a **finger-access relief** or tool slot adjacent the latch arm, permitting deliberate release of the latch (e.g., for reconfiguration or disassembly) by manual or tool-assisted deflection of the arm, so that the frame halves can be repositioned to a different recess if reconfiguration is required after initial assembly.

The recesses themselves may be configured as **through-slots** (visible/inspectable from the exterior, permitting visual confirmation that the latch is fully seated) or as **blind pockets** (concealed, providing a cleaner external appearance and improved EMC shielding continuity across the joint).

### 6. Additional Alignment and Anti-Rotation Features

To ensure that engagement occurs squarely and that the two frame halves cannot be joined in an unintended skewed or misaligned orientation, the joining walls preferably additionally include:

- **Longitudinal guide rails and grooves** running parallel to the insertion direction, engaging complementary rails/grooves on the mating joining wall, so as to constrain relative motion to a single translational degree of freedom (along the array of recesses) prior to latching;
- **Stop tabs or end walls** at the extremities of the recess array, defining the maximum and minimum relative positions available, and preventing over-insertion past the last recess;
- **Index markings** (e.g., embossed numerals or ribs adjacent each recess) allowing an assembler to visually confirm and record which relative position/recess has been selected, for repeatability in production.

### 7. Alternative Embodiments

- **Symmetric/identical half construction:** In one embodiment, the first and second frame halves are of identical molded construction (mirror-symmetric or rotationally symmetric), each half provided with both a press projection and a complementary recess array at opposite ends, such that two identical parts can be joined to each other (reducing part count to a single tooling design).
- **Multiple projection/recess sets:** Additional press-projection/recess-array pairs may be provided along the side walls (in addition to, or instead of, the base/joining wall), to further stabilize the joint against bending or torsional loads.
- **Shielding continuity:** Where the frame halves are provided with a conductive (metallized or metal-insert) shielding layer, the press projection and recess surfaces may additionally be configured to make direct metal-to-metal contact upon latching, preserving electromagnetic shielding continuity across the joint irrespective of which recess position is selected.

---

## Advantages

1. Enables a single pair of (or a single, identical) molded frame-half components to serve a range of assembled lengths/module capacities, reducing part variety and tooling cost.
2. Provides a robust, tool-less, positive latch connection without separate fasteners.
3. Permits fine or coarse adjustment of relative frame-half position
